method: heuristic-v1 news-only; no AIS or historical market corroboration
limitations: Label validity requires human review of the cited sources.
Windows within an event are correlated; report event counts as well as window counts.
These are news-only metrics, not measured performance of the combined AIS system.
Publication-date proxies and paraphrased source text do not establish real historical ingestion or warning lead time.
Undefined metrics are null, not evidence of perfect performance.
Research event links supply context only; CSV risk labels are not converted into disruption ground truth. Only the separately source-reviewed pilot windows are scored.

cases.label_rationale: EIA documents shipping diversion away from Bab el-Mandeb and the Red Sea after attacks, with longer routes and increased travel time. Label target is an already documented shipping disruption, not a complete strait closure.

extractions.evidence: Red Sea shipping attacks divert oil cargoes around Africa.

cases.label_rationale: EIA reports a substantial reduction in petroleum flow through Bab el-Mandeb and diversion after attacks. This window belongs to the same event family as the June case and is not an independent event.

extractions.evidence: Bab el-Mandeb oil traffic falls as Red Sea attacks disrupt shipping.

cases.label_rationale: The June 16 EIA report explicitly says maritime traffic through Hormuz had not been blocked despite regional tensions. This is a non-blockage control as of that report, not proof that shipping faced no geopolitical risk.

extractions.evidence: Hormuz oil shipping continues during regional tensions.
